texts.facts: : The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident. 2. The brief contents of the petition are as under: On 23.10.2021 at about 10.00 pm., when the petitioner was travelling in a bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 from Vokkaligara Samudhaya Bhavana S.S.Ghati Tobagere Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk near Happy Valley resorts, the driver of the bus drove the same with a very high speed, recklessness and suddenly dashed to the road safety guard at right side but fell down. Due to said impact, the petitioner and other passengers were forcibly knocked down and were sustained multiple grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital Doddaballapura wherein he took treatment as an SCCH - 9 3 MVC No.450/2022 inpatient for 5 days and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards his treatment and nourishment. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was doing Coolie and agriculturist work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month. The accident in question occurred due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B- 9051 by its driver and the jurisdictional Doddaballapura Rural police have registered a case in their crime No.287/2021, after investigation the said police have filed a charge heet against the said driver, punishable under Section 279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC. The first respondent being the insurer and the second respondent being the policy holder of said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- under all heads together with interest and costs. 3. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.1 SCCH - 9 4 MVC No.450/2022 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and have filed their respective written statement. 4. The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent. Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner. Respondent contended that, Manjunatha P.N vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 18 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38722345/ 2 compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant. Further denied the involvement of Bus bearing No.KA-06-B-9051 in the alleged accident. Further contended that, driver of the Bus was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident. Further contended that, the said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-060B-9051 was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident. Further the respondent No.1 has contended that, the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act. Respondent admitted the SCCH - 9 5 MVC No.450/2022 issuance of policy of insurance in favour of second respondent in respect of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy. Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.1 prayed to dismiss the petition against it. Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
